title: Truthfulness Truthfulness
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child states why we tell the truth: truthful lips last for ever but a lying tongue only a moment (Proverbs 12:19); Ephesians 4:25 tells Christians to put off falsehood and speak truthfully, even when the truth is hard.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the story of Ananias and Sapphira.
floor.question: What did Ananias and Sapphira lie about?
floor.answer: The money from the land they sold

representations: two columns: truth lasts, lies do not
story cards of children owning up
steps: What lasts? Truth. What does not? A lie.
Own up, even when it is hard.
contexts: a test mark shown to parents

board.do: Write Proverbs 12:19 and draw two lines, one long and one short.

board.say: Which lasts only a moment, truth or a lie?

board.do: Wait for the child to say a lie.

misconceptions.ask: You broke a cup by accident. What should you say?
misconceptions.repair: Role-play telling the truth and the parent's kind answer.
Write it on a flash card: truth lasts, lies do not.

misconceptions.ask: A child failed a test and is ashamed. What should he tell his father?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what the father can do once he knows.

listen_for: Yes, I did not say anything false
misconceptions.ask: Your friend is blamed for the broken window you broke, and you say nothing. Is that truthful?
misconceptions.repair: Act it out: who is punished? Speaking truthfully to your neighbour (Ephesians 4:25) means owning up.

checks.question: What does Proverbs 12:19 say lasts for ever?
You broke a cup by accident. What should you say?
checks.answer: It was me, and I am sorry
